messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: SEV2 - runtime latency spike in us-west-2 after deploy 'fastflip' (deploy_id=df-2026-03-17-09). P95/P99 token latency increased, errors rising. Auto-alerts triggered.
oncall-alex: On it. Eng paging and looking at metrics now.
eng-runtime-sam: I see a pattern in runtime logs starting ~09:12 UTC: repeated kernel selector fallbacks. Example log: `kernel=kv_fallback reason=selector_mismatch instance=rt-2345`.
sre-maria: Eviction counts on the GPU pool spiked at the same time. Prefetch queue depth jumped; batching window went from ~8ms -> ~120ms which explains tail latency.
product-raj: Are customers impacted? CS seeing a few timeout reports. Need ETA on mitigation.
support-lydia: Confirmed — 3 customer tickets referencing timeouts on generation endpoints (#7891, #7894, #7896). CS notified.
eng-runtime-sam: Quick mitigation: flip the canary feature flag to route traffic off the canary variant (fastflip.canary_enabled -> false). That should avoid the new selector path. Requesting oncall approval to flip.
oncall-alex: Approve the flip. Do it and report status. If no improvement in 5m, prepare for full rollback.
eng-runtime-sam: Running command now: ```/opt/releasectl flip fastflip.canary_enabled false --deploy-id=df-2026-03-17-09 --reason='selector fallback surge'```
infra-bot: Deploy bot: feature flag flip accepted, traffic shift initiated at 09:18:22 UTC.
incident-bot: Automated: traffic shifted from canary -> stable variant (shift %) completed. No full rollback executed.
sre-maria: Monitoring metrics: p99 latency dropping from ~2.6s -> ~0.9s over the next 3 minutes. Eviction rate trending down. Prefetch queue depth normalizing.
support-lydia: Notified affected customers that we mitigated and are monitoring. Will update tickets after stable 30m.
product-raj: Do we still need to rollback the release? What's the risk of leaving the release in stable path?
eng-runtime-sam: Root cause looks like an unintended selector tweak in canary binary that causes inefficient kernel selection under our workload distribution. The stable variant is fine. My recommendation: keep the release toggled off for canary traffic, patch selector logic, run an internal micro-canary, then reenable carefully. No full rollback required now.
oncall-alex: Agreed. No rollback for now. Please prepare a short postmortem and action items. Handing off follow-ups to eng-runtime. @eng-runtime-sam taking lead.
eng-runtime-sam: Taking lead. Action items: 1) RCA on selector change + unit tests (sam), 2) add pre-deploy synthetic check for kernel selector/eviction regression (maria), 3) customer comms draft and ticket updates (lydia/product). Will open CR/PR within the hour.
infra-bot: Runbook/reference: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/canary-kernel-selector (internal).
sre-maria: Also recommend adding a canary-only metric alarm for eviction count > threshold so we catch this earlier during rollout.
oncall-alex: Handoff note: my oncall shift ends in 20m. If latency resurges, page SRE and re-escalate. Leaving thread in eng-runtime's hands.
eng-runtime-sam: :thumbsup: Opening CR now and will post links here.
support-lydia: I'll update customers after stable 30m and add a summary to their tickets.
incident-bot: Incident recorded as SEV2-2026-03-17-0945. Timeline and follow-ups will be appended to the incident doc. Closing immediate paging.
